---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose common Plate setup and runtime issues.
---

Most Plate issues come from version skew, duplicate React/Plite runtimes, or
crossing the server/client import boundary. Start with package alignment, then
check runtime ownership, then inspect plugin resolution with `DebugPlugin`.

## Start here

| Symptom | First check |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid hook call, null dispatcher, or React hook crashes. | Duplicate `react` / `react-dom` or mixed package-manager installs. |
| Plugins render as plain text or components do not attach. | Missing plugin, wrong `/react` versus base import, or wrong component map. |
| Server Component crashes on import. | A Server Component imported `platejs/react` or `platejs/<feature>/react`. |
| `requires disabled plugin` in the console. | An explicitly disabled plugin is required by an enabled plugin. |
| `Pass a plugin descriptor, not its name.` | A dependency contains a string instead of a plugin descriptor. |
| Markdown, HTML, or static rendering misses nodes. | The static/base plugin kit does not include the serializer or node plugin. |

Use the focused guide when the issue belongs to one area:

| Area | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Editor creation and options | [Editor](/docs/plate/editor) |
| Plugin configuration | [Plugin](/docs/plate/plugin) |
| Plugin store state | [Plugin Context](/docs/plate/plugin-context) |
| Debug logging | [Debugging](/docs/plate/debugging) |
| Server Components | [RSC](/docs/plate/installation/rsc) |
| Static rendering | [Static Rendering](/docs/plate/static) |

## Update Plate

Plate editor features ship from one `platejs` package. Use the Plate CLI to
update it without managing a set of feature package versions.

```bash
npx @platejs/cli@latest deps platejs --latest --install --yes
```

For pnpm projects:

```bash
pnpm dlx @platejs/cli@latest deps platejs --latest --install --yes
```

Then inspect what actually resolved.

```bash
npm ls platejs react react-dom
```

```bash
pnpm why platejs
pnpm why react react-dom
```

If the tree shows multiple Plate majors, align the Plate packages first. If it
shows multiple React copies, fix the package that pulls the extra copy
instead of papering over the tree with a random override.

## Fix runtime boundaries

Use React entrypoints only in client-side editor code.

| Runtime | Import from |
| --- | --- |
| Editable React editor | `platejs/react`, `platejs/<feature>/react` |
| Server Component static output | `platejs/static`, `platejs`, `platejs/<feature>` |
| Node script or route handler without React UI | `platejs`, `platejs/<feature>` |

<Callout type="warning" title="No React plugins on the server">
  Server Components and Node scripts should not import `platejs/react` or
  `platejs/<feature>/react`. Use base plugins such as `BaseHeadingPlugin` from
  `platejs`, not `HeadingPlugin` from `platejs/react`.
</Callout>

If a server route only needs serialization or transforms, use the Node path from
[Node.js](/docs/plate/installation/node). If it renders read-only React output, use
[Static Rendering](/docs/plate/static).

## Check component wiring

When a node appears as plain text or a default `div`, check the component path.

```tsx title="components/editor/plugins.tsx" showLineNumbers
import { HeadingPlugin } from 'platejs/react';

import { HeadingElement } from '@/components/editor/heading';

export const plugins = [HeadingPlugin.configure({ component: HeadingElement })];
```

For copied Plate UI kits, inspect the kit that owns the feature before adding
manual component overrides. Feature kits usually wire plugins, components,
shortcuts, and options together.

| Component surface | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| Copied registry components | [Plate UI](/docs/plate/installation/plate-ui) |
| Feature-owned kits | [Feature Kits](/docs/plate/feature-kits) |
| Manual node components | [Plugin Components](/docs/plate/plugin-components) |

## Inspect plugin resolution

Enable `DebugPlugin` when plugin state, dependencies, or runtime behavior do
not match what the editor receives.

```tsx title="components/editor/plugins.tsx" showLineNumbers
import { DebugPlugin } from 'platejs';

export const plugins = [
  DebugPlugin.configure({
    initialState: {
      logLevel: 'warn',
    },
  }),
];
```

Common debug errors:

| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `requires disabled plugin` | An enabled plugin requires a dependency that the app disabled. |
| `Circular plugin dependency` | Plugin dependencies form a cycle. |

Use [Plugin](/docs/plate/plugin#advanced-plugin-configuration) to check `dependencies`,
`enabled`, and `override.*` behavior.

## Reset the install

When the dependency tree looks correct but the runtime still behaves like two
React or Plite copies are loaded, reinstall from the existing lockfile.

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
npm install
```

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
pnpm install
```

Delete the lockfile only when you intentionally want a fresh dependency
resolution. That is a package-management decision, not a Plate fix.

## Report a reproduction

When you open an issue, include the smallest editor that reproduces the problem:

- Package manager and lockfile type.
- Output from the relevant `npm ls` or `pnpm why` commands.
- The plugin list passed to `useCreateEditor`, `createEditor`, or
  `createStaticEditor`.
- The failing value, if the issue depends on document content.
- The exact error message from `DebugPlugin` or the browser console.

Small reproductions beat screenshots. The package tree and plugin list usually
tell the story.
